chunks: Muhammad ibn Ahmad narrated from al-Haytham ibn al-Nahdi, from al-Hasan ibn Mahbub, from Ali (peace be upon him)

Regarding a man who gave another man dirhams to perform Hajj on his behalf as a single Hajj, he said: 'He is not permitted to perform Tamattu' (combining Umrah and Hajj) with the Umrah to the Hajj, so as not to differ from the owner of the dirhams.'

The explanation of this report is one of two matters: One is that he is given the choice, it is permissible for him to perform either of the two Hajjs, and neither is obligatory upon him over the other, just as Tamattu' is obligatory upon him if he performs Hajj for himself. The other is that the latter report is specific to one whose obligation is Ifrad (single Hajj); it is not permissible for him to be performed for as a Mutamatti', because that does not suffice for him. And the first applies to one whose obligation is Tamattu'; so if he gave for Ifrad and differed to the Tamattu' which is his obligation, it suffices for him.
On the condition that the latter report is suspended (mawquf) and not fully connected (ghayr musnad), and a report like it is not objected to against the fully connected reports.

key_terms.صَاحِبُ الدَّرَاهِمِ: The owner of the dirhams (the one who paid)
key_terms.مَوْقُوفٌ: Suspended (a report ending with a companion)
key_terms.مُسْنَدٌ: Fully connected (a report ending with the Prophet or Imam)

ai.seo_question: What is the ruling if someone pays a proxy to perform Hajj on their behalf regarding the type of Hajj performed?
ai.summary: Shaykh al-Tusi analyzes the validity of a proxy performing Tamattu' on behalf of an obligator bound to Ifrad, resolving the apparent contradiction between connected and suspended reports by distinguishing between the proxy's personal obligation and the specific requirements of the delegator. This juristic nuance highlights the Shia emphasis on precise adherence to the type of Hajj (Ifrad vs. Tamattu') when fulfilling the religious duty of others, ensuring the act is valid for the specific individual it represents.
